endpoints.review: The subject explicitly names the species.
An efficiency or plant-trait parent preserves the distinction from phosphorus uptake.
Experimental nutrient exposure is worth checking, but the background sentence only asserts optimal supply. A chemical entity changes the meaning.
Quality of starch is the measured quality concept.
Growth is a broader process covering root growth.
The source explicitly reports decreased network width.
Medium is a category assigned by this study. Classifying it as a general increased-size trait would discard the category definition.
Low phosphorus is an experimental exposure regimen here. The broader class leaves the level in the claim.
The measured root length stays distinct from root surface area.
Area is broader than root surface area. Root cross-sectional area measures a different feature.
The dry root mass measurement supports the root dry-weight candidate. Mass is usable only as a broader classification.
Check whether the shortage denotes the experimental exposure and whether the cited evidence specifies phosphate. Preserve the restriction.
A generic ratio is defensible. A length-to-length ratio would require evidence for the measurement basis.
The study describes a specific category of root systems. The hierarchy does not identify the studied category itself.
The class denotes lateral roots and the source retains the restrictive quantity.
The specific uptake observation is for the small rooting type.
The named cultivar is a member of the species. Preserve the cultivar context.
Total root length is a root-system morphology trait. The definition of length of a root does not establish identity with total system length.

relations.review: A significant difference between treatment groups is not a reported correlation.
Significance of the genotype-by-treatment interaction does not assert a correlation.
The source uses affects without asserting the conditions of a specific approved causal property.
